title: Roman Mythology and Its Relation to Greek Myths
text: Roman mythology encompasses the traditional stories pertaining to ancient Rome's legendary origins and religious system. Roman mythology heavily borrowed from Greek mythology, though the gods were given Latin names: Zeus became Jupiter, Hera became Juno, Poseidon became Neptune, Athena became Minerva, Ares became Mars, Aphrodite became Venus, and Hermes became Mercury. The Romans added their own myths, particularly concerning Rome's foundation: according to tradition, Romulus and Remus were twin brothers raised by a she-wolf; Romulus killed Remus and founded Rome in 753 BCE. The Aeneid by Virgil, written around 29–19 BCE, connected Rome's origins to the Trojan War hero Aeneas, a son of Venus.
